x: Also on the programme was a 440 yards open to unattached novices, and this was won by J. Murphy, with Coxon second and Roffey third. We hope these lads have now joined the club and wish them every success for the future.
Roffey and Bagnall gave of their best whilst Dave Baulch ran above form and forced himself past Ingles in the home straight to make sure we had six men home before T.V.H. had three.

Burr gained a place but Bagnall was passed by Ken Norris, T.V.H. who did 17.42, the fastest time of the day. Walker gained two places and Roffey put us in the lead. Bedford ran last and was caught by Knight of Essex.
Cliff Roffey running in his first Brighton for us was next and though running well, was passed by Hames, Essex who established a new course record of 25mins.

Jack continued his fine running of this road season and finished only 10 yards behind Reed and in so doing beat the old course record by 15 seconds. Walker then conceded 30 seconds to Peter Pirie and Roffey finishing, had little chance of catching Morgan of S.L.H.

Llewellyn of Walton won the mile in 4.24.2, closely followed by Davidson and Roffey. Alan Sexton, despite having had a skinful for dinner, was cajoled into running 220 yards which he won with comparative ease in 23.7s Nice to see you back on the track Alan.

On paper we had high hopes of being second to Portsmouth AC but once again we were unable to field a truly representative team and the ten that did start were dogged by misfortune.Those that were unable to appear were Linstead (injury), Thresher (cold), Newell (work) and Roffey (flu).
